reasons: Load and error paths are handled, with a retry button and a route to the live tool.
No test or other evidence of correct behaviour is visible in this file.
Matching a selection depends on the server sending the project list; without it the file shows a notice instead of a result, which is safe but limits the demo.

terms.meaning: Showing a result that was saved earlier, step by step, without doing the work again.
The saved copy of one demo run that the server keeps for replay.
The set of industries, segments, companies or projects a run covers.
The exact list of project ids a recorded run covered.
A React function that stores state or fetches data for a component.

sections.name: File setup, DemoTool, QA
sections.title: Purpose notes and imports
sections.what: Explains the rules of the demo in a comment, imports the parts it needs, and defines the two supported tools and the shape of a saved question and answer.
sections.why: The comment states the rules, so later changes can be checked against them; the rest is setup.
sections.watch_out: The comment is the only written rule set, so any change must keep replay free of live calls.

sections.name: PreparedPresentation, fmtDate, norm, LIVE_HREF
sections.title: Shape of a recorded run
sections.what: Describes everything saved for one recorded run: tool, run id, date, scope, deck, questions, amendment, stages, hints, source checks and research.
sections.why: Defines what the server must supply so the demo can replay the run.
sections.watch_out: Many fields are optional, so code that reads them must handle their absence.

sections.name: usePrepared
sections.title: Loading the recorded run
sections.what: Fetches the saved run for one tool from the server and keeps it, so it is not requested again while the page is open.
sections.why: Likely reason: a recording never changes, so keeping it avoids repeat requests.
sections.watch_out: The cache never goes stale, so a corrected recording only appears after a page reload.

sections.name: preparedScope
sections.title: Recorded selection in picker form
sections.what: Converts the saved selection into the shape the scope picker uses, filling any missing lists with empty ones.
sections.why: Lets the recorded selection use the same picker controls as a live selection.
sections.watch_out: Missing lists become empty, so a partly saved selection can look broader than it was.

sections.name: usePreloadedScope
sections.title: Preloading the recorded selection
sections.what: On demo entry, places the recorded selection into the picker once, and only if the picker is still empty.
sections.why: So the first screen already matches the recording.
sections.watch_out: A page reload resets the one-time guard, so the recorded selection will be applied again.

sections.name: cohortIds, ScopeMatch
sections.title: Possible match results
sections.what: Lists the recorded project ids and defines three outcomes: match, unavailable, or mismatch with counts.
sections.why: Lets the screen say whether the current selection is the recorded set.
sections.watch_out: If the server does not send the project list, the outcome is unavailable, never a match.

sections.name: matchCohort
sections.title: Comparing selection with recording
sections.what: Counts projects in the recording but not on screen, and on screen but not in the recording, and reports a match only when both counts are zero and the recording is not empty.
sections.why: An exact set comparison prevents replaying a result that does not fit the selection.
sections.watch_out: An empty recorded list never counts as a match.

sections.name: useReplayMatch
sections.title: Shared match hook for index pages
sections.what: Used by both tool index pages to load the recording, compare it with the shown projects, and open the replay page.
sections.why: Keeps the matching and navigation rules in one place for both tools.
sections.watch_out: The comparison runs only when demo mode is on and a list of shown project ids is supplied.

sections.name: ReplayScopeNotice
sections.title: Selection notice and restore action
sections.what: Shows in the selection panel whether the current selection matches the recording; if not, explains what was recorded and offers a restore button or a live run button.
sections.why: Tells the visitor plainly that a changed selection has no recorded result instead of silently showing a different one.
sections.watch_out: The live run button appears only when an action is passed in, and the text warns that a live run can take several minutes.

sections.name: describeScope
sections.title: Readable description of a selection
sections.what: Writes a short plain summary of a selection from its industries, segments, companies and project count, falling back to the saved label.
sections.why: Gives the visitor a human description of what was recorded.
sections.watch_out: If none of those parts are present, the saved label is shown instead, which may be vague.

sections.name: scopeIsEmptyLocal
sections.title: Empty selection check
sections.what: Returns true when no industries, segments, projects or companies are selected.
sections.why: Used to decide whether there is anything to preload or restore.
sections.watch_out: Peer and research settings are ignored, so a selection that holds only those looks empty.

sections.name: toResearchSources
sections.title: Converting saved sources for display
sections.what: Turns saved source references into the source format the assistant panel expects, marking each as fetched or search only.
sections.why: Likely reason: the assistant panel uses its own source format, and this adapts the saved one.
sections.watch_out: The fetched status is inferred only from whether a web address exists; the page itself is not checked.

sections.name: reverifyQA
sections.title: Re-verify reply from stored checks
sections.what: Builds the reply for the re-verify action from checks stored at recording time, stating for each source whether its quote was found then, and saying nothing was re-checked now.
sections.why: Keeps the replay honest by reporting the recorded checks, not new ones.
sections.watch_out: When no checks were stored, the function returns nothing and the caller tells the visitor a live run is needed.

sections.name: ReplayMessage
sections.title: Replay chat message type
sections.what: Describes a saved chat message that can also carry its original source references.
sections.why: Lets the replay keep sources while the Scan panel ignores the extra field.
sections.watch_out: Any new consumer of these messages must tolerate the extra field.

sections.name: useReplayAssistant
sections.title: Replay chat answers
sections.what: Answers chat prompts only from stored text: it runs the re-verify, edit or recorded research reply, or matches a suggested question to its recorded answer, and otherwise says no model runs in replay.
sections.why: The comment says unrecorded prompts must not receive generated answers.
sections.watch_out: Matching uses normalised text, so a reworded question gets the honest no-recorded-reply message.

sections.name: download
sections.title: File download helper
sections.what: Fetches a file from the server, saves it to the browser's download link and frees the temporary link after two seconds.
sections.why: A file fetched with request headers needs a temporary link before the browser can save it.
sections.watch_out: A failed fetch is not caught here, so the caller must handle errors.

sections.name: preparedRows
sections.title: Saved stage rows for display
sections.what: Converts each saved stage into the row format the live views use, shows a missing status as not reported, and removes the recipe field from summaries.
sections.why: The comment says a missing status must not look complete, and the recipe could lead to opening and changing the saved run.
sections.watch_out: Only the summary loses its recipe field; the log is still shown as text.

sections.name: preparedStages
sections.title: Stages for the progress view
sections.what: Builds the stage list for display: for Reality Scan it uses the scan stage builder and hides the body of the final stage; for Lessons Learnt it uses the stage labels and pairs them with the saved rows by position.
sections.why: Keeps the replay looking the same as a live run.
sections.watch_out: Lessons stages are matched by position, so a change in stage order would mislabel them.

sections.name: ReplayBar
sections.title: Replay top bar
sections.what: Shows the recorded date, scope and project count, a note that statuses are as recorded, any local changes, Reality Scan download buttons, a skip button, a discard button and a link to run live.
sections.why: Tells the visitor they are watching a recording and which changes exist only on screen.
sections.watch_out: Download buttons appear only for Reality Scan, so Lessons Learnt has no downloads here.

sections.name: LoadState
sections.title: Loading and error message
sections.what: Shows placeholder bars while the recording loads, and on failure a message with a retry button and a link to the live tool.
sections.why: Gives the visitor a way forward when the recording cannot be loaded.
sections.watch_out: The live link depends on the tool name, so a new tool needs its own live route.

sections.name: ScanReplayView
sections.title: Reality Scan replay entry
sections.what: Shows the Reality Scan replay body once the recording has loaded, otherwise the loading message.
sections.why: Waits for the recording before drawing anything, so no empty screen appears.
sections.watch_out: The screen depends on the loading state being correct; a stuck load shows only placeholders.

sections.name: useReplayDeck
sections.title: Shared replay state
sections.what: Holds the local state for both demos: whether the amendment was requested, its decision, text edits and chart cut. It builds the deck the slide editor shows, the actions the editor can call, and a reset.
sections.why: Keeps the local-only behaviour in one place so the export matches what the visitor sees.
sections.watch_out: Edits are keyed by element id, so two edits sharing an id would overwrite each other.

sections.name: preparedExport
sections.title: Prepared presentation download
sections.what: Asks the server for the saved presentation with local changes attached and downloads it as a PowerPoint file, named with the tool and whether it was edited.
sections.why: Lets the visitor take away the replayed deck as it looks on screen.
sections.watch_out: The changes are sent as text in the web address, so a very large set of edits could exceed address length limits.

sections.name: ScanReplayBody
sections.title: Reality Scan replay body
sections.what: Shows the recorded process first, using the same progress view as a live run, then reveals the slide editor when the process finishes or the visitor skips.
sections.why: Follows the live experience without faking any new work.
sections.watch_out: The deck appears only after the process has been shown, and a recording with no trace lines skips straight to the deck.

sections.name: LessonsReplayDeck
sections.title: Lessons slides replay entry
sections.what: Shows the recorded Lessons Learnt deck in the editor once it has loaded, otherwise the loading message, and passes along an optional deck connection.
sections.why: Lets the Lessons tab reuse the same editor as a live run.
sections.watch_out: Whether the optional deck connection could save to the live service is unclear from this file, so it should be checked before use in replay.

sections.name: LessonsReplayBody
sections.title: Lessons replay body
sections.what: Shows the recorded Lessons Learnt deck with a note about the recording date, a list of local changes, and a discard button after any change.
sections.why: Makes clear that the deck is a recording and that edits stay on screen.
sections.watch_out: The discard button appears only once a local change exists.

summary: Lets a visitor replay a pre-recorded LNG demo of the Reality Scan and Lessons Learnt tools without starting any new server work.
purpose: Gives a demonstration path that shows a saved run in the same screens as a live run, while making no new runs, research or model calls.
why: The header comment says replay must not start runs, research or model calls, and must not change a saved deck or the Yard, so local state is kept on screen and only exported.
how: First, `usePrepared` loads the recorded run from the prepared endpoint. `usePreloadedScope` puts the recorded selection into the picker once, and `useReplayMatch` with `matchCohort` checks whether the visible selection is the recorded project set. For Reality Scan, `ScanReplayBody` replays the recorded stage logs in `AgentProcess` and then shows the slide editor. For Lessons Learnt, `LessonsReplayBody` shows the recorded deck. Edits, the chart cut and the amendment decision are kept in `useReplayDeck`. `useReplayAssistant` answers chat prompts only from stored replies. `preparedExport` downloads the deck with those local changes.
inputs: The prepared run from the guided-demo prepared endpoint, the demo and replay URL flags, the picker's current selection, and the visitor's actions (typing edits, applying or dismissing the amendment, asking prompts, exporting).
outputs: Rendered replay screens, a short list of local changes, chat replies from the recording, and a downloaded PowerPoint file.
risks: A recorded result can look live if its label is missed. A wrong match could show a result for a different selection. Local edits can be mistaken for saved edits, and the export is a plain file download with no error handling in `download`.
debug: If the replay says no recorded result for this scope, compare the selection with the recorded project list in `matchCohort`. If the recording fails to load, check the response from the prepared endpoint and the message in `LoadState`. If a prompt gets no recorded reply, check the question text against the stored questions in `useReplayAssistant`. If an export is wrong, check the options passed to `preparedExport`.
